Thanks Tessa — quick read of the external redline (I pulled the doc). Two technical/legal points we should propose as counters:

1) Roles and liability: The customer's redline tightens Processor obligations and adds a clause that treats Redwood as a "Joint Controller" for certain downstream processing. We should reject joint controller framing and keep Redwood as Processor. Proposed language: short clause that preserves Processor status and describes the limited purposes of processing tied to the Order Form.

2) Transfer impact addendum / residency carveout: Horizon's draft requires that certain EU-origin data not be routed through US-based queues during failover. That's effectively a geo-routing requirement. If they insist, that triggers either Private deployment (regionally pinned infra) or a significant uplift in price to cover geo-locked capacity and testing. Our customer-facing alternative: (a) sign SCCs + an explicit subprocessor assurance schedule + certified KMS/HSM key controls, and (b) we provide an operational runbook for emergency DR transfers with notification and rollback windows.

I added suggested markup lines in the doc: see comments on pp. 4-6. Also note we can offer a 30-day post-sign subprocessor list commit (standard). If Horizon requires pre-sign full list discretion, escalate to Sales Ops.

—Karthik

On Wed, Sep 8, 2026 at 08:14, Elena Morales <elena.morales@horizoncare.com> wrote:
> Hi Tessa — attaching HorizonCare's counsel redline to the DPA and a clean Order Form with our annotations. Two immediate asks: (1) we need confirmation that Redwood can commit to Processor role limits as drafted ...

Team — draft customer-facing language (two bullets) below that we can send back to HorizonCare. I'm proposing we:

• Confirm Processor status and limited purposes: "Redwood will act as a Processor with respect to Customer Personal Data processed under the Order Form. Redwood processes Customer Personal Data only to provide the Services as set out in the Order Form and as instructed by Customer. Redwood shall not act as a Controller of Customer Personal Data except to the extent required by applicable law, in which case Redwood will notify Customer unless prohibited by law."

• Offer transfer safeguards in lieu of geo-locking: "Where Transfers outside the EEA are necessary, Redwood will: (i) execute the European Commission's SCCs (or equivalent); (ii) maintain a current Subprocessor Schedule and provide it within 30 days post-signature; and (iii) maintain key-management and access controls (KMS/HSM) and audit evidence upon reasonable request. For disaster recovery scenarios that may temporarily route traffic via alternate regions, Redwood will provide advance notice and an operational rollback plan; where Customer requires hard geo-locking for specific datasets, Redwood will discuss a Private deployment option and associated commercial impact."

Commercial/ops note: If Horizon requires pre-sign full subprocessor visibility or binding geo-locking, Sales should prepare an exception request and cost memo.

Happy to refine wording for Elena.

—Laura Bennett
